newsitem.title: USA: Barney's to close some stores in cost-cutting plan.
newsitem.headline: Barney's to close some stores in cost-cutting plan.

text.p: Barney's Inc., the upscale retailer whose rapid expansion and partnership woes led to bankruptcy court, said Tuesday it planned to close its famed Seventh Avenue and 17th Street store here as part of a cost-cutting plan.

The retailer, which carries haute couture for both men and women, said it will also close stores in Dallas and Houston, as well as in Troy, Mich. It will trim costs at its New York headquarters and at its Lyndhurst, N.J., distribution centre.
Company President John Brincko said the company had no choice but to close the stores because they were performing poorly.

The company said it will continue to operate three major stores in New York, Chicago and Beverly Hills; five regional stores and a smaller store at the World Financial Centre in New York City as well as 10 outlet stores throughout the country.
Brincko said many employees affected will be offered positions at the remaining stores.
The store on 17th Street in Manhattan is expected to close in September while the others will be closed by the end of July, the company said.

With the closures and other cost-cutting, Barney's will employ about 1,750 workers in nine stores in New York City and Manhasset, N.Y.; Beverly Hills and Costa Mesa, Calif.; Chicago; Chestnut Hills, Mass.; Westport, Conn., and Seattle.
The number will also include those retained at the 10 outlets and the New Jersey distribution site.

Barney's was founded in 1923 by Barney Pressman, grandfather of current Barneys executives Gene and Robert Pressman. The store, which once was known as Barneys Boy's Town, has under the guidance of the younger Pressmans evolved into a retailer known for top-line fashion and high-priced accessories.
However, critics of the company have said Barney's overextended itself in its expansion plans, especially with its store on Manhattan's pricey Madison Avenue.
In that store, the company poured heavy resources into building a luxurious trophy to compete with the exclusive boutiques nearby, run by top French and American apparel designers.
Brincko said earnings of the Barney's chain "significantly improved" recently and the closings as well as other cost-cutting efforts will speed up such improvement.
"Our reorganization strategy is proceeding on a timely, positive track," he said.

Barney's filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in January 1996 amid a dispute with its former partner, Japanese retail group Isetan Co. Ltd. The two retailers have sued and countersued each other over millions of dollars in partnership loans.
Dispute over $50 million from the partnership and a 1989 agreement that set an ambitious expansion plan for the United States and Asia led Barney's to bankruptcy court.
In March, Hong Kong retailer Dickson Concepts Ltd. offered to buy the chain for $240 million, but the bid was rejected by creditors, who said it was too low.
Barney's has also attracted interest from other retailers, according to Wall Street analysts.
